events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

message.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

args.content:
# Books

A small reading list. No accounts, no database — books live in one JSON file.

```sh
npm start          # http://localhost:3000
npm test
```

- `PORT` — port to listen on (default `3000`)
- `BOOKS_FILE` — where to save (default `data/books.json`, created on first add)

## What you can do

| Page | |
|---|---|
| `/` | what you're currently reading, what you've finished, and the add form |
| `/books/:id` | one book: title, author, your notes — a plain URL, so it's shareable as-is |

Marking a book finished moves it to the finished shelf; the book's own page can move it
back to reading. Notes can be written when you add a book and edited any time afterwards.

## Layout

    src/store.js    the JSON file: read, add, mark finished, save notes
    src/views.js    HTML rendering (everything user-typed is escaped)
    src/app.js      routing and form handling
    src/server.js   reads PORT / BOOKS_FILE and listens

Pages are rendered on the server and forms are plain HTML forms, so there is no build
step and no client-side JavaScript. Writes go through a queue and are saved by writing a
temporary file and renaming it, so two quick submissions can't lose each other's book and
an interrupted save can't truncate the library.

events.content:
Done. `npm start` → http://localhost:3000.

**What it does**
- `/` shows two shelves — Currently reading and Finished — with the add form (title, author, optional notes) underneath. Each reading book has a "Mark finished" button right in the list.
- `/books/:id` shows title, author, status, and your notes. Notes are editable there, and the book can be moved back to reading if you finish one by mistake.
- That book URL is a plain server-rendered page with no session or cookie behind it, so pasting it to someone just works. There's a test that fetches one as a cookie-less client to keep it that way.
- Books are saved to `data/books.json` (override with `BOOKS_FILE`); I verified persistence by killing the server and reading the list back from a fresh process.

**How it's built** — zero runtime dependencies, just Node's `http` module and HTML forms. No build step, no client-side JS, nothing to install beyond what was already here. Four files: `src/store.js` (the JSON file), `src/views.js` (HTML), `src/app.js` (routes), `src/server.js` (listen).

Two details worth knowing about, both cheap and both covered by tests: saves are serialised and written via temp-file-then-rename, so two fast submissions can't lose each other's book and an interrupted write can't truncate the library; and everything you type is HTML-escaped, since a title like `<script>…</script>` would otherwise execute on the page you share.

29 tests pass (`npm test`). One thing I decided rather than asked: the add form takes notes up front and the detail page lets you edit them — notes had to get in somehow for the detail page to show them, and that seemed like the least surprising route. I left out deleting books, since you didn't ask for it; say the word if you want it.
